title: The Solomon–Yau least-volume theorem
coverage: I read the full LaTeX source in build/sections: introduction, preliminaries, index, minmax, family, cones and conclusion. Checks by hand: (1) Lemma clifford-ratios: the log-convexity of d_j via the trigamma and midpoint-convexity bound. Numerically, theta_m is about 1.571, 1.540, 1.5, 1.487 and so on for m=2..11, so it is strictly decreasing, theta_4 = 3/2, and every value is below 2. (2) Immersion reduction by cone monotonicity. (3) The two-point curvature maximum, Lemma index-upper-tests. I re-derived the first-derivative relation s*phi_i = (phi - lambda_i)*d_i, the reflected normal n_y (unit length and orthogonal to y and to T_y Sigma), and the reflected frame inner products. I recomputed Delta_x Z, Delta_y Z and the mixed terms; the cancellation to s(Delta phi + (P-m)phi) - (2/s)*Sum (phi - lambda_i) d_i^2 is correct. In the diagonal case I checked the unit-field Laplacian formula, the optimal choice of beta, and the Codazzi step T_{1i} = phi_i. Then the Poisson-comparison proof of the integral of P being at least m|Sigma|. (4) Perdomo/Li–Yau index rigidity: the conformal area derivative identity, the spectral sum giving the integral of P at most m times the integral of beta^2, pointwise equality P=m, and the Clifford classification. (5) Min-max: filling double cover; the detection gap via the odd map to R^{m+3}, where p = m+3 components force a zero (Borsuk–Ulam); gamma_m > sigma_m from the hemisphere centroid; and how the Marques–Neves discretization, Almgren extension and homotopy-class lower bound fit together. (6) Lorentz family: the inverse-boost formulas, the differential dY = O(rI - hA), the level cover Lambda contained in Y(T), the AM–GM bound det(rI - hA) <= r^m, monotonicity and compactification of the graph, the boundary-antipodal complement condition and the central loop (empty set to full sphere), no concentration at finite and infinite boosts, strict loss through the truncated determinant on a fixed patch (including t_*=1), the central tube, and the Morse-type deformation using an extra L-eigenfunction eta with B positive definite on W plus R*eta. (7) Cone induction: splitting off the radial line, the base case k=1 (N<3 for m>=4; N even via cyclicity for m=2,3; triple-junction density 3/2 is not below theta_m), the use of the outer induction for links of dimension 3..m, preservation of mod-2 cyclicity under blow-ups and slicing, exact mass in the attainment limit, and the final contradiction. I did not re-verify the cited black boxes (Allard, White 2009, Marques–Neves Theorems 2.14/3.9/3.10/3.12) beyond checking that their stated hypotheses match how they are used.
main_claim: For every m>=2, every closed connected minimal immersion F: M^m -> S^{m+1} whose image is not totally geodesic has volume, counted on the domain with multiplicity, at least a_m, the least volume of a minimal Clifford product S^k(sqrt(k/m)) x S^{m-k}(sqrt((m-k)/m)). This is the Solomon–Yau conjecture.
